findings.summary: FeatureTypeBadge component signature changed from {type} prop to full Feature object, but two callers in CheckAccess.tsx (lines 184, 199) were not updated and still pass type={val}. Non-Boolean features will display 'single use' badge instead of the correct type.
findings.failure_scenario: Onboarding with metered features: selectedFeature.type is 'metered', passed as {type:'metered'} to FeatureTypeBadge. The new component reads feature.config?.usage_type which is undefined (no config prop passed). Falls through to 'single use' display. User sees wrong feature type label in the onboarding CheckAccess step.

findings.summary: Debugging console.log(cusContext) left in production code, leaks the full customer context object (potentially including customer data, features, env info) to the browser console.
findings.failure_scenario: Any page load in the customer detail view triggers `useCustomerContext()` then logs it. Customer data (IDs, feature assignments, product states) appears in browser devtools for any user who opens the console, violating data hygiene expectations.

findings.summary: Debugging console.log('feature', feature) left in production code, will fire on every render of the FeatureTypeBadge component and spam the console with full feature objects.
findings.failure_scenario: FeaturesTable renders a row per feature; FeatureTypeBadge is called once per row. Every render cycle logs all feature data to console, producing noisy output and potentially leaking feature config details.

findings.summary: React 'Check' and 'Track' code snippet templates call useCustomer() hook at module level instead of inside a React component function, teaching users invalid hook usage patterns.
findings.failure_scenario: User copies the displayed example code (const { allowed } = useCustomer() at module level) into their own React component. React throws 'Invalid hook call' / 'Hooks must be called inside a function component' error. The old snippet wrapped hooks inside an export default function component.

findings.summary: FeatureTypeBadgeProps interface is defined but never used after the component signature was changed to accept (feature: Feature) directly. Dead code.
findings.failure_scenario: Maintainers reading the code see the interface and may assume it is the contract, leading to confusion about the actual component interface. Unused interface adds noise.

findings.summary: Nine lines of the old JSX implementation left as commented-out code after the rewrite, creating dead-code maintenance burden.
findings.failure_scenario: Future maintainers spend time wondering whether the commented code should be deleted, whether it's kept as a reference for a planned revert, or whether they should follow it as a pattern. Adds visual noise and diff clutter.

findings.summary: The Check icon import from lucide-react is no longer used after replacing inline button logic with the ToggleButton component. Dead import.
findings.failure_scenario: Build tooling (tree-shaking) may or may not remove it. In stricter linting environments this becomes a build error. Adds unnecessary dependency reference.
